source.title: How Fragile Is Safety Alignment at Frontier Scale? A Single-Direction Attack on a 320B MoE
source.authors: Yi Shi; Tan-Yu Chen; Kai Shen

record.file_problem: The text begins with a clipped fragment, but contains the paper through its conclusion, limitations, references, and appendix.
record.tranche_reason: Applies the original difference-in-means direction and rank-one weight-projection recipe to a new model, and measures refusal and capability outcomes. It also tests the practical baked weight edit.
record.gate_note: The paper directly tests rank-one ablation and reports outcomes. Related-work results cited from other papers are not recorded. Layer-selection scores, direction-estimation sweeps used to select settings, and quantization engineering measurements are omitted because they do not report the target refusal or capability behavior as a finding of the intervention.
record.test_reason: Applies the original recipe unchanged to a 320B MoE (GLM-5.3-Flash): last-token difference-in-means direction, rank-one projection of all residual writers. It measures harmful refusal, false refusal and capability, with a random-direction control and rank-2 and category-subspace extensions. It also bakes the edit into the released block-FP8 checkpoint, which tests V2. It does not test V3 (jailbreaks suppressing the direction, robustness training) or V6 (cross-language, cross-variant or base-to-instruct transfer). Applying the recipe to a new model is not V6 transfer.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that rank-one ablation removes 41–89 points of refusal on seven benchmarks with no detected capability change. They find a random orthogonal direction leaves refusal unchanged, and editing writers beats layer-boundary projection. Name-matching implementations fail silently, reaching 0.066 of 0.776. They state that what carries the resistant residue is unknown and that generalization beyond this one model is unmeasured.
record.recipe_differences: The authors describe the recipe as unmodified: last-token difference of means and a rank-one projection. Applying it required structural enumeration of fused experts, collapsing the multi-stream activation for direction estimation, and iterative dequantize-project-requantize editing of block-FP8 weights.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on editing all writer groups jointly: 74% of the full effect appears only under the joint intervention. Writer editing removes more refusal than layer-boundary projection on paired prompts. Refusal reductions vary by benchmark and content category. Layer 22 was selected using a validation comparison; the paper reports non-monotonic variation across candidate layers. Higher-rank subspace conditions also vary in unfinished-response rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Under manifold-constrained hyper-connections, cross-stream mixing is scalar per stream, so writer-level orthogonalization keeps every stream and every read orthogonal to r. Tensor-parallel ranks give identical residuals.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Directional ablation remains valid in multi-stream residual architectures whose mixing does not rotate within the hidden dimension.

record.problems: One model only; no human refusal annotations; capability evaluation uses four sampled benchmarks and has no power analysis; greedy decoding has reported run-to-run variation; only one random orthogonal-direction control; subspaces at ranks 1–12 were independently fitted with randomized SVD and selected minima are exploratory; unfinished responses rise at higher ranks and can lower REFUSAL-only rates; the editing implementation is withheld, so the results cannot be reproduced by downloading the code.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row cap, omitted the rule-classifier repeats for Table 7 and Table 8; extra writer-hook harmful/harmless label counts; the rank-sweep rule-classifier rates and unfinished-response rates; and the numerical block-FP8 iteration/leakage comparisons. These are in §§4.4, 5.2, 5.4–5.5 and Appendix A; the selected primary judge outcomes and direct behavior measures are retained.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts. Thinking mode (all runs at reasoning_effort=low). Models other than GLM-5.3-Flash. Multiple random-direction controls.
Other released models; an independent public implementation (code withheld).
Entirely untested: no prompt jailbreak is analysed for direction suppression, and no training against ablation.
Affine versus cone geometry. A nested-basis rank comparison (ranks fitted independently).
Entirely untested: no cross-language, cross-variant or base-to-instruct transfer of the direction.
Untested. The paper states thinking mode is untested; think blocks were stripped at low reasoning effort.

missing.what: Baked-versus-hook gap from FP8 requantization leakage: hook predicts 0.031; baked gives 0.188 at 8 iterations and 0.094 at 32. Attention-only: hook 0.812 vs baked 0.828.
Rule-classifier rates for the baked edit (e.g. SR 0.273, SST 0.340 vs judge 0.380, 0.480), showing scorer dependence of the residual.
Harmless-prompt refusal under the writer-subset hooks: 5/100 unedited, 0 with all three groups edited.
Layer dependence: layers 20 and 22 effective, layer 25 not; non-monotonic across depth 0.4–0.8.

record.verdict_notes: V3 and V6 links were removed throughout. The record treats the ablation itself as the 'jailbreak' and the new model as 'transfer', but V3 concerns other attacks acting via the direction, and V6 concerns carrying a direction across languages, variants or training stages. Hook experiments (r16–r34) are not weight edits, so they are not V2, except r20, which simulates the name-matching implementation. Reference-condition rows r16, r25 and r26 are baselines, not results. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Tests one direction on one model and reports harmful refusal, harmless false refusal, and four sampled capability benchmarks. It does not test adding the direction to induce harmless refusals.
Tests a baked weight edit on one released checkpoint only; it does not test other released models or an independent implementation.
Tests the direction-ablation attack's effect on harmful-request refusal. It does not test other jailbreaks suppressing the direction or training against ablation for robustness.
Tests category-specific residue and subspaces through rank 12. It does not distinguish an affine mechanism from a cone or establish the geometry of the surviving refusal.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment versus refusal decision.
Tests one frontier-scale MoE model. It does not test cross-language transfer, multiple model variants, or transfer from a base checkpoint to an instruct checkpoint.
No comparison of safety-training methods, data, or timing.
The paper states that thinking mode is untested; evaluation uses reasoning_effort=low.

relation.reason: Its own results bear on whether the versions hold: baked and hooked ablation with before/after refusal rates, a random-direction control, a writer-group decomposition, a writer-vs-boundary paired comparison, and a rank sweep. It does not merely use the direction as a tool.

tranche.reason: The recipe is the original's, unchanged and stated as such: last-token difference of means over harmful/harmless prompts, normalized, and one rank-one projection of every residual-writing weight, with no training, gradients or second direction. The measure is refusal rate on harmful benchmarks plus XSTest over-refusal and capability. The structural changes (enumerating fused experts, collapsing four streams, iterated FP8 orthogonalization) are handling needed to apply the same method, not a different method.

source_check.notes: All 25 row values, baselines, subjects, conditions and states check out against Tables 5-10; the one soft call is r32's 'partial' beside r31's 'absent' for comparable rank-2 moves. Two things a researcher must carry: (1) the random-direction control, the rank-2 extensions and the rank 1-12 sweep are inference-time hooks at layer 22 on all 132 writer sites, not the baked edit, and their rank-1 comparators are 0.320 (SR) and 0.190 (JBB) with no confidence intervals, so quoting them beside the baked 0.380/0.150 (as V1.support[0], V1.suggested_status, V2.method_sensitivity[5] and the reading-list entry do) mixes conditions; (2) Section 4.4's 'lossless hook predicts 0.031' does not reconcile with Table 7's all-writer hook rate of 0.173 on the same 256 held-out prompts, so the 0.094-vs-0.031 requantization gap should be quoted with that caveat. Housekeeping: rows r02-r06, r10, r17 and several Table 8 rows still carry V3/V4/V6 links although the study measures no jailbreak mechanism and no transfer, contradicting the record's own V3/V6 untested lines. No text in the study addresses an AI reader; the harmful-content material is benchmark names and category labels only.
